final_answer:
Let
\[
\Delta_\tau(\lambda)=\lambda+1+a e^{-\lambda\tau}+b e^{-2\lambda\tau}
\]
be the characteristic function. For this linear retarded delay equation, the zero solution is globally asymptotically stable exactly when all zeros of \(\Delta_\tau\) have negative real part.

For small \(\tau>0\) this is true: if \(\Re\lambda\ge0\) and \(\Delta_\tau(\lambda)=0\), then
\[
|\lambda+1|\le a+b,
\]
so such roots are bounded; letting \(\tau\to0\) would force a limiting root of
\[
\lambda+1+a+b=0,
\]
which has negative real part. Thus instability for some \(\tau\) can occur only by a crossing through a nonzero imaginary root.

Put \(\lambda=i\omega\), \(\omega>0\), and \(\theta=\omega\tau\). Then
\[
i\omega+1+a e^{-i\theta}+b e^{-2i\theta}=0.
\]
Separating real and imaginary parts gives
\[
1+a\cos\theta+b\cos 2\theta=0,
\]
\[
\omega=a\sin\theta+b\sin 2\theta.
\]
Writing \(c=\cos\theta\), the real equation becomes
\[
P(c):=2bc^2+ac+1-b=0.
\]
If \(P(c)=0\) for some \(c\in(-1,1)\), then one can choose \(\theta\) with \(\cos\theta=c\) so that
\[
a\sin\theta+b\sin2\theta
=\sin\theta(a+2bc)>0,
\]
except in the exceptional case \(a+2bc=0\). But that exception forces \(b=1\), and then
\[
P(c)=2c^2+ac=c(2c+a),
\]
so \(c=0\in(-1,1)\) is another root giving a positive imaginary crossing. Hence stability for every \(\tau>0\) is equivalent to
\[
P(c)>0\qquad\text{for every }c\in(-1,1).
\]

Now analyze
\[
P(c)=2bc^2+ac+1-b,\qquad b>0.
\]
Its vertex is at
\[
c_*=-\frac a{4b}.
\]

If \(0<b\le\frac13\), then the condition is exactly
\[
a\le 1+b.
\]
Indeed, if \(a>1+b\), then \(P(-1)=1-a+b<0\), while \(P(1)=1+a+b>0\), so \(P\) has a root in \((-1,1)\). Conversely, if \(a\le1+b\), then either \(a\ge4b\), in which case the minimum on \([-1,1]\) is at \(-1\) and \(P(-1)\ge0\), or \(a<4b\), in which case
\[
P(c_*)=1-b-\frac{a^2}{8b}>0
\]
because \(a^2<16b^2\le8b(1-b)\). Thus no interior root exists.

If \(b>\frac13\), then \(a\ge4b\) already implies \(a>1+b\), producing an interior root. Therefore we need \(a<4b\), so the vertex lies in \((-1,1)\), and the condition is
\[
P(c_*)=1-b-\frac{a^2}{8b}>0.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
b<1,\qquad a^2<8b(1-b).
\]

Therefore the required set of parameters is
\[
\boxed{
\left\{(a,b):0<b\le\frac13,\ 0<a\le1+b\right\}
\ \cup\
\left\{(a,b):\frac13<b<1,\ 0<a<\sqrt{8b(1-b)}\right\}.
}
\]
